Eurostat data stories

125 news items · 9 statistical themes · 2020–2021 · six stories revisited with today’s data

From 2020 to 2021 I was a statistical consultant for a company contracted by Eurostat to produce its “What’s New” news items. I did the statistics, analysed the data and wrote 125 articles, including items on migration and asylum, disability, equality and living conditions. Eurostat set the topic and the dataset for each item. My work was the analysis, the quality checks, the writing, and the review rounds with Eurostat.

Many of those stories were written with data that ended in 2018–19, or in the middle of the pandemic. Here I revisit six of them with the latest Eurostat data, and this time I make the charts myself, in R. Each case study follows the same structure: what was published → what I explored further → working with the data → design choices → code.

What this project shows

Working with official statistics. Finding the right dataset, and handling flags, breaks in series, revisions and EU aggregates that change over time (EU-28 to EU-27).

Data quality. Checking my own calculations against the figures Eurostat publishes, and noting what the data can’t tell us.

Writing statistics for the public. Short, accurate text for readers who are not statisticians.

Reproducible analysis in R. Every chart is made from the downloaded data with one script, using tidyverse and ggplot2.
